outcome.shown: A bicycle stays upright primarily through a combination of rider input and self-stabilizing mechanical design. While the gyroscopic effect of the spinning wheels provides a minor stabilizing force, the most significant factor is the bike's geometry—specifically the "trail," which is the distance between where the steering axis hits the ground and where the tire makes contact. This design causes the front wheel to naturally steer into the direction of a lean, allowing the rider to steer underneath the bike's center of mass to correct their balance. Ultimately, the rider’s constant, subtle micro-adjustments to the handlebars are what maintain equilibrium, keeping the bicycle upright even at low speeds.
